[re-verdict 2026-10-25, kb/Work PB929, measured on this build (cobol.exe --std 2002, free form); it replaces the record of kb/Work PB388, whose two 'unreachable' alternatives were written before kb/Work PB496 (the objectReferenceUsage spellings) and PB389 (the object-reference descriptor) landed]
Citations validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "an object reference described with an interface-name that identifies int-1 or an interface inheriting from int-1"` -> OK 10) a); `"if described with a FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10) b) 1.; `"if described without a FACTORY phrase, the objects of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10) b) 2.; `"if described without a FACTORY phrase, the objects of the class containing the data item referenced by identifier-4 shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10) c) 2.; `"the predefined object reference NULL"` -> OK 10) e).

EVERY ALTERNATIVE OF SR10'S CLOSED LIST IS REACHABLE AND PINNED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. One table decides them: ObjectReferenceSet.Refusal, which OoConformance.ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch asks for a SET, a RETURNING delivery and a BY CONTENT argument, and OoBinder.OoBindSetObjectRef calls for the SELF and NULL senders. The two alternatives the former record called unreachable are not: USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF class-name and USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE [FACTORY OF] ACTIVE-CLASS are the first two alternatives of objectReferenceUsage (CobolOO.g4, kb/Work PB496), and ObjectRefDescriptor carries the FACTORY, ONLY and ACTIVE-CLASS axes (kb/Work PB389), so b) 1. asks the FACTORY closure (ImplementsClosure(sc, send.Factory)) rather than hard-wiring the instance one, and c) asks the class that CONTAINS the sender. The old complaint about a fixed 'SR12' tail on every rejection is gone too: each arm prints its own sub-rule.
- a) an interface sender that identifies or inherits int-1. ACCEPTED: pb929_set_sr10_interface_receiver_senders (SET RI TO RJ, RJ described with PB929J, which INHERITS FROM the receiver's PB929I; INVOKE RI "PING" prints PING-C). REFUSED: pb929-set-sr10-interface-sender-unrelated -> COBOL0867 'interface P9A1Z neither identifies nor inherits from interface P9A1I (ISO §14.9.39.3 SR10 a))'.
- b) 1. a class sender WITH a FACTORY phrase whose FACTORY object implements int-1. ACCEPTED: pb389_object_reference_descriptor (SET R TO F). REFUSED: pb929-set-sr10-factory-sender-not-implementing -> COBOL0867 'the factory object of class P9B1C does not implement interface P9B1I (ISO §14.9.39.3 SR10 b)1.)'; the class's INSTANCE half implements the interface and its FACTORY half does not, so a check that asked the instance closure accepts the program.
- b) 2. a class sender WITHOUT a FACTORY phrase whose objects implement int-1 (a subclass of an implementing class included). ACCEPTED: pb389_object_reference_descriptor (SET R TO B). REFUSED: pb929-set-sr10-class-sender-not-implementing -> COBOL0867 'the objects of class P9B2C do not implement interface P9B2I (ISO §14.9.39.3 SR10 b)2.)'.
- c) 1. and 2. an ACTIVE-CLASS sender, with and without FACTORY. ACCEPTED: pb389_object_reference_descriptor (SET FIR TO FA in factory method FMK, SET IR TO A in method MK). REFUSED: pb929-set-sr10-active-class-sender-not-implementing -> COBOL0867 'the objects of the class containing the ACTIVE-CLASS sender (P9C2C) do not implement interface P9C2I (ISO §14.9.39.3 SR10 c)2.)'.
- d) 1. and 2. SELF in a factory or an instance method: ACCEPTED oo_set_self_interface and pb451_set_format5_self_sender; REFUSED oo-set-self-interface-not-implemented and pb451-self-sender-factory-not-implements.
- e) NULL: ACCEPTED pb929_set_sr10_interface_receiver_senders (SET RI TO NULL; IF RI = NULL prints NULLOK after RI held a real object). NULL conforms to every object reference (§13.18.60.4 GR22: an object reference 'shall contain either null or a reference to an object'), so it has no refusing direction.
- The universal sender is in none of the lists: ObjectRefDescriptorDriftTests.EveryTypedShape_RefusesAUniversalSender proves all seven typed receiver shapes refuse it.

[folded SR-14.9.39.3-L4.1 = §14.9.39.3 10) d) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB451 — WAS PARTIAL on a REFUTED reading; the refutation is itself refuted here, from the standard, and the row CLOSES. Rule: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "if the SET statement is contained in a method within the factory definition of the class, that factory definition shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1"` -> OK 10) (SR10 d)1.). THE INTERPRETIVE QUESTION, DECIDED FROM THE SPEC: is 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1' a LITERAL claim about the clause's operand list, or the standard's prose for the SS11.4.4 GR2 relation? It is the relation, on four independent grounds. (1) SS11.4.4 GR1: 'The IMPLEMENTS clause specifies the names of the interfaces that are implemented by the factory object of the containing class ACCORDING TO 9.3.11, Interface implementation' - the clause is defined in terms of implementation, not the reverse. (2) SS9.3.8.2.3 rule 5 b)2.a. states the SAME obligation about the SAME objects with the OTHER phrasing: 'if described with the FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-r', where SET SR10 b)1. writes 'the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1'. Two phrasings, one rule. (3) Annex D (SS D.19.5) paraphrases SS13.18.60.4 GR22 c) - normatively 'the object referenced by this data item shall IMPLEMENT interface-1' - as 'the data item can only be used to reference an object DESCRIBED WITH AN IMPLEMENTS CLAUSE THAT REFERENCES the interface specified': the standard glosses its own rule with the other spelling. (4) The reductio: under the literal reading, in a subclass whose own definition carries no IMPLEMENTS clause, `SET R TO SELF` would be illegal while `SET T TO SELF` (T typed at the containing class) followed by `SET R TO T` is legal under SR10 b)2. - identical semantics, one statement apart. MEASURED (pb451_set_format5_self_sender): the FMK method's `SET JR TO SELF` exercises GR2 a)+b) (FACTORY IMPLEMENTS PB451K, which INHERITS PB451J, the receiver's int-1) -> FPING-P; PB451Q's QFMK exercises GR2 c) (PB451Q's FACTORY carries NO IMPLEMENTS clause at all; only its base's does) -> FPING-Q. The REFUSING arm is pinned for the first time by pb451-self-sender-factory-not-implements, whose discriminator is the factory/instance axis - the INSTANCE definition implements the interface and the FACTORY definition does not, so a screen keyed on the wrong definition accepts it. || CODE SITE: OoBinder.OoBindSetObjectRef, the SELF arm's ObjectRefKind.Interface case -> OoClassTable.ImplementsClosure(cur, host.OoInFactory), which is exactly SS11.4.4 GR2 a)+b)+c).

[folded SR-14.9.39.3-L4.2 = §14.9.39.3 10) d) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB451 — WAS PARTIAL on the same REFUTED reading as L4.1, on the INSTANCE arm; CLOSED for the same reason and by the same argument (see SR-14.9.39.3-L4.1's note for the four grounds, all from the standard). Rule: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "if the SET statement is contained in a method within the instance definition of the class, that instance definition shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1"` -> OK 10) (SR10 d)2.). The relation is SS11.8.4 GR2 - a) a direct IMPLEMENTS clause, b) an implemented interface that INHERITS intf-1, c) an inherited class whose instance object implements it - and SS11.8.4 GR1 defines the clause through it ('the interfaces that are implemented by the object of the containing class according to 9.3.11'). MEASURED: the existing pair oo_set_self_interface / oo-set-self-interface-not-implemented pins the DIRECT leg in both directions; the two legs it never reached are now pinned by pb451_set_format5_self_sender - MK's `SET J2 TO SELF` over GR2 b) (OBJECT IMPLEMENTS PB451K, which INHERITS the receiver's PB451J) -> IPING-P, and PB451Q's QMK over GR2 c) (PB451Q's OBJECT carries NO IMPLEMENTS clause; its base PB451P's does) -> IPING-Q. Both were the programs the prior REFUTED note cited as evidence of over-permissiveness (its r01 and r02); re-derived from SS11.8.4 GR2 they are CONFORMING programs, and refusing them would reject legal source. || CODE SITE: the same call, with host.OoInFactory false. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Oo/OoConformance.cs#ObjectRefWideningMismatch (ObjectRefWideningMismatch was renamed ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch (kb/Work PB389, 2b2e38a47))
